concepts.title: Sound as a Longitudinal Wave
concepts.body: Sound is a type of longitudinal wave that requires a medium, such as air, water, or solids, to propagate. In longitudinal waves, particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation. For example, when you speak, your vocal cords create vibrations that travel through the air as sound waves.

concepts.title: Frequency, Wavelength, Amplitude, Pitch, and Loudness
concepts.body: Frequency is the number of vibrations per second, measured in Hertz (Hz). Wavelength is the distance between two consecutive compressions or rarefactions. Amplitude is the maximum displacement of particles from their mean position. Pitch is determined by frequency—higher frequency means higher pitch. Loudness depends on amplitude—greater amplitude means louder sound. For instance, a guitar string vibrating faster produces a higher pitch, while plucking it harder increases its loudness.

concepts.title: Reflection of Sound and Echo
concepts.body: When sound waves strike a hard surface, they bounce back, a phenomenon known as reflection. Echo is the repetition of sound caused by the reflection of sound waves from a distant surface. For example, shouting in a large empty hall produces an echo as the sound reflects off the walls.

formulas.title: Wave Speed Formula
formulas.body: v = f x lambda (v in m/s, f in Hz, lambda in m). Here, v is wave speed, f is frequency, and lambda is wavelength. This formula is used to calculate the speed of a sound wave in a medium.

formulas.title: Echo Distance Formula
formulas.body: d = v x t / 2 (d in m, v in m/s, t in s). Here, d is the distance to the reflecting surface, v is the speed of sound, and t is the time taken for the echo to return. This formula is used to determine the distance of an object based on the time taken for an echo to return.

examples.title: Everyday Example: Hearing a Doorbell
examples.body: When someone rings a doorbell, sound waves travel through the air and reach your ears. The cause of hearing the sound is the vibration of the doorbell creating sound waves that propagate through the air.

examples.title: Applied Example: Ultrasound Imaging
examples.body: In medical ultrasound imaging, high-frequency sound waves are sent into the body, and their reflections are used to create images of internal organs. The cause of the image formation is the reflection of sound waves at different tissue boundaries.

mcqs.question: What type of wave is sound?
mcqs.explanation: Sound is a longitudinal wave because particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation. Transverse waves involve perpendicular vibrations, electromagnetic waves do not require a medium, and surface waves occur at the boundary of two media.

mcqs.question: If the frequency of a sound wave is 500 Hz and its wavelength is 0.68 m, what is its speed?
mcqs.explanation: Using the formula v = f x lambda, v = 500 Hz x 0.68 m = 340 m/s. The correct answer is 340 m/s, as the other options do not match the calculated value.

mcqs.question: A person claps and hears an echo after 3 seconds. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, how far is the reflecting surface?
mcqs.explanation: Using the formula d = v x t / 2, d = 340 m/s x 3 s / 2 = 510 m / 2 = 170 m. The correct answer is 170 m, as the other options are incorrect calculations.
